contracts.commit_point: The first host filesystem access after _resolve in each tool, which the guard must precede: fp.read_text (read_file libagents/tools/files.py:64; read_summary libagents/tools/files.py:128), fp.write_text (write_file libagents/tools/files.py:152; edit_file libagents/tools/files.py:185), and fp.unlink (delete_file libagents/tools/files.py:196).
contracts.declared_mechanism: PathMapper.to_host strips the env_root/host_root prefix, resolves the remainder against host_root, and raises ValueError unless the resolved path equals host_root or is one of its parents (libagents/paths.py:72-84); the tools' _resolve wraps to_host and re-raises as ToolError so the tool call fails closed before touching the filesystem (libagents/tools/files.py:9-13).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A resolved host path that is neither the environment root nor beneath it (a path escaping host_root), i.e. any file operation targeting a location outside the environment root; to_host raises ValueError("path escapes the environment root: ...") exactly when resolved != host_root and host_root not in resolved.parents (libagents/paths.py:82-83).
pending_binding_information: The reviewer claims the HTTP API files endpoint and _safe_ui_candidate enforce the same confinement; libagents/api.py is not among the supplied views, so operator-side binding is unverified.
Whether other host-side writers (board tools, memory writes outside libagents/tools/files.py) route through PathMapper.to_host is not shown in the supplied views.
contracts.protected_operation: The host filesystem accesses of the five agent file tools operating on agent-supplied paths: read_file and read_summary reads, and write_file/edit_file creates-overwrites and delete_file unlinks, each of which first calls _resolve(ctx, args["path"]) (libagents/tools/files.py:56, 125, 149, 173, 191).
contracts.protected_resource: The host filesystem outside the environment root (everything not under PathMapper.host_root, which is the resolved environment directory, libagents/paths.py:68-84).
contracts.protection_obligation: Agent-invoked file tools (read_file, read_summary, write_file, edit_file, delete_file) must refuse to resolve any agent-supplied path outside the environment root before any host filesystem access, via PathMapper.to_host raising on escape and the tools' _resolve converting that refusal into a ToolError that aborts the call.
scope_limits: Only effects routed through _resolve/PathMapper.to_host are covered; any file effect that does not call to_host is outside this contract.

read_file/read_summary are non-mutating reads; they are included because the same guard gates them, while the stratum reflects the mutating tools (write_file, edit_file, delete_file) whose commit points are cited.
Shell commands are not subject to PathMapper; filesystem confinement for shell commands is a separate sandbox-level mechanism (README.md:227-231), covered by the macOS Seatbelt contracts.
The guard is resolution-time; whether it is raced by concurrent path swaps is not assessable from the supplied source.

contracts.commit_point: The sandbox-exec process spawn inside MacOSSandbox.exec: the persistent session shell created with self._argv("/bin/bash", ...) (libagents/sandbox.py:486-495) and the one-shot subprocess.run(self._argv("/bin/bash", "-lc", command), ...) (libagents/sandbox.py:497-504); the deny-by-default profile attaches at that spawn and governs all writes of the sandboxed process tree.
contracts.declared_mechanism: MACOS_SEATBELT_PROFILE: (deny default) with (allow file-write* (subpath (param "ENV_ROOT"))) plus the narrow cache exceptions (libagents/sandbox.py:207-249); bound to every command via _argv, which builds sandbox-exec -D ENV_ROOT=... -D DARWIN_TEMP/... -p MACOS_SEATBELT_PROFILE ... (libagents/sandbox.py:451-461); fail-closed availability check _require_seatbelt raises RuntimeError when not on darwin or /usr/bin/sandbox-exec is missing (libagents/sandbox.py:441-449, invoked from start/exec).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A sandboxed subprocess writing or deleting any host file outside the ENV_ROOT subpath, apart from the explicitly allowed narrow caches (xcrun_db, CFNetworkDownload_*, NSIRD_swift-* under DARWIN_TEMP; the Xcode PlugInCache under DARWIN_CACHE; the DARWIN_METAL_CACHE subpath), as declared in the profile's deny-default plus scoped file-write allowances (libagents/sandbox.py:207-249) and the MacOSSandbox contract statement (libagents/sandbox.py:427-430; README.md:236-238).

Allowances contributed by the imported fragments system.sb and com.apple.corefoundation.sb (libagents/sandbox.py:210-212) are not visible in the supplied source and could affect the effective write policy.
Runtime effectiveness of the Seatbelt regex rules cannot be verified from source alone.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of shell commands by MacOSSandbox.exec, covering both the persistent-session shell and the one-shot command path, each wrapped in sandbox-exec with the profile (libagents/sandbox.py:480-510).
contracts.protected_resource: The host filesystem outside the environment root, where the boundary is the resolved environment directory bound as the ENV_ROOT profile parameter (libagents/sandbox.py:438-439, 455).
contracts.protection_obligation: Shell commands executed under the macOS sandbox must be denied host filesystem writes and deletions outside the environment root (the ENV_ROOT subpath), except the narrow filename-scoped Swift/Xcode/Metal cache allowances, by the deny-by-default Seatbelt profile applied at every sandbox-exec invocation of MacOSSandbox.exec, failing closed when sandbox-exec is unavailable.
scope_limits: Reads are deliberately broad ((allow file-read*)) and network access is allowed (libagents/sandbox.py:215, 256); only writes/deletions are confined.
Filename-scoped cache exceptions permit writes under DARWIN_TEMP, DARWIN_CACHE, and DARWIN_METAL_CACHE per the regex/subpath rules (libagents/sandbox.py:218-249).
Declared best-effort against accidental damage from trusted agents, not a security boundary for hostile code (libagents/sandbox.py:9-11; README.md:239-240).
Applies only to MacOSSandbox; LocalSandbox has no isolation (libagents/sandbox.py:13-15; README.md:229-231) and Docker relies on container isolation instead.
Seatbelt is Apple-deprecated and may change; the mode fails closed when sandbox-exec is unavailable (README.md:240-242; libagents/sandbox.py:441-449).

contracts.commit_point: The sandbox-exec process spawn inside MacOSSandbox.exec: the persistent session shell via self._argv(...) (libagents/sandbox.py:486-495) and the one-shot subprocess.run(self._argv(...)) (libagents/sandbox.py:497-504).
contracts.declared_mechanism: The same MACOS_SEATBELT_PROFILE deny-by-default registration bound per command through _argv's sandbox-exec -p invocation (libagents/sandbox.py:207-216, 451-461), with fail-closed availability via _require_seatbelt (libagents/sandbox.py:441-449); the profile enumerates allowances without any signal grant, so signalling falls to deny default.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A sandboxed subprocess sending signals to host processes unrelated to the sandboxed process tree; declared at libagents/sandbox.py:427-431 and README.md:238, and enforced by the profile's (deny default) with no signal allowance, the only process-target allowance being process-info* restricted to target self (libagents/sandbox.py:208-209, 251-252).

The allowance set contributed by imported Seatbelt fragments is unknown from the supplied views, so the exact effective signal policy cannot be fully confirmed.
contracts.protected_operation: Execution of shell commands by MacOSSandbox.exec (persistent-session and one-shot paths), each spawn wrapped in sandbox-exec with the deny-default profile (libagents/sandbox.py:480-510).
contracts.protected_resource: Host processes outside the sandboxed process tree (unrelated host processes).
contracts.protection_obligation: Shell commands executed under the macOS sandbox must be denied from signalling unrelated host processes, via the deny-by-default Seatbelt profile applied at every sandbox-exec invocation of MacOSSandbox.exec.
scope_limits: Signal denial derives from (deny default) plus the absence of a signal allowance; imported Apple fragments (system.sb, com.apple.corefoundation.sb) could add allowances not visible in the supplied source (libagents/sandbox.py:210-213).
process-info* is allowed only for target self (libagents/sandbox.py:252); process-fork and process-exec within the sandbox are allowed (libagents/sandbox.py:251).
Declared best-effort guard against accidental damage, not a hostile-code boundary; applies only to MacOSSandbox (libagents/sandbox.py:9-11; README.md:239-240).
